title: [Performance] Optimize EP gather and reduce operations for uniform SP layout and DP=1
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? On FlashComm SP-MoE topologies (dp=1, TP8/EP8), every MoE layer calls the `vllm::maybe_all_gather_and_maybe_unpad` custom op 3x and `vllm::maybe_pad_and_reduce` 1x. Profiling (torch profiler, eager prefill) shows these ops account for ~23% of the prefill step, and the time is dominated not by the collectives but by identity tensor reconstruction inside the ops: - **AG side**: when `local_sizes` is uniform (dp=1 always is: `ceil(N/tp)` repeated), the code gathers into a `(tp, N, d)` buffer and then does `view + 8x select + cat(8 complete slices)` — a bit-identical copy of the gathered tensor (one extra `aten::empty` + `CatArrayBatchedCopy`). - **RS side**: symmetrically, `_maybe_pad_and_reduce` allocates `zeros((tp, max_len), ...)` and copies all rows in (one `fill` + one full-tensor copy), then `reduce_scatter(...).narrow` slices off padding that is zero-width for dp=1 — an identity rebuild. This PR adds fast paths: 1. **Uniform `local_sizes`**: AG returns the gathered tensor directly (row-major identity of the cat); RS calls `reduce_scatter(x, 0)` directly (the trailing `narrow` is a no-op when uniform). 2. **dp=1 without `local_sizes`** (legacy chunked path): AG replaces `empty + row-copy` with a zero-copy view slice of the fresh gather output; RS replaces `zeros + copy` with a single `F.pad`. 3. The non-uniform path (dp>1 with uneven split across DP ranks) is kept unchanged. Semantics are unchanged: for uniform sizes the removed ops were provably identity operations; outputs are bit-identical, and the -1/zero padding contract is untouched. Per-op profile (same topology, steady-state prefill step): | Op | Before | After | Delta | |---|---|---|---| | `vllm::maybe_all_gather_and_maybe_unpad` (per call) | 670 us | 367 us | -45% | | `vllm::maybe_pad_and_reduce` (per call) | 1.870 ms | 397 us | -78% | The remaining 367 us per AG call is the collective itself plus host framework, confirming the reconstruction overhead (not the collective) was what got removed. ### Profile Before: After: ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? No. No config or API change; performance-only, outputs bit-identical. ### How was this patch tested? - New unit tests in `tests/ut/ops/test_register_custom_ops.py`: uniform AG/RS pass-through, dp=1 and dp=2 no-`local_sizes` fast paths, and uneven-size cases guarding the unchanged slow path. - Trace verification on a steady-state prefill step: after the patch the op subtrees no longer contain `aten::cat` / `aten::zeros(fill)` / `aten::select` and contain no extra `aten::copy_`; only the collective and host framework remain. - E2E benchmark above; long-run stability run on the same topology. Env: 8x Ascend 910B, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W4A8, TP8/EP8, dp=1, FlashComm v1, FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Dataset: 46.5k-token shared prefix + 3.5k random suffix, 350 output tokens, concurrency 6, server-side sampling. | Metric | Before | After | Delta | | Metric | Before | After | Delta | | ------------------------------------ | -------- | -------- | ----- | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2534.87 | 2509.38 | -1.0% | | Median TTFT (ms) | 2398.52 | 2385.69 | -0.5% | | P99 TTFT (ms) | 8432.48 | 8362.36 | -0.8% | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 34.91 | 32.66 | -6.4% | | Median TPOT (ms) | 34.44 | 32.23 | -6.4% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 38.60 | 36.35 | -5.8% | | Mean E2EL (ms) | 14719.05 | 13908.99 | -5.5% | | Median E2EL (ms) | 14444.76 | 13626.27 | -5.7% | | P99 E2EL (ms) | 19844.93 | 19002.31 | -4.2% | | Output token throughput (tok/s) | 140.06 | 148.23 | +5.8% | | Peak output token throughput (tok/s) | 199.00 | 204.00 | +2.5% | --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change involves boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max values, off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable, I added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`. - [ ] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression test that would fail without the fix. - [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths (exceptions, timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path. - [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior and are not written merely to satisfy CI. - [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive path, I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
